entries.title: Tell the estate the moment this repository pushes a record
entries.detail:
graph.yml in flashyos merges every property's fragment on a daily
schedule, so without a dispatch a change here is invisible to the estate
for up to 24 hours — and "the graph is a day behind" is
indistinguishable from "this property has nothing new to say".

The dispatch has been in the shiplog/backlog template since August and
in no repository, because each vendored its workflow before the template
had it. This adds it, gated on the commit step having actually pushed: a
dispatch per run rather than per change would turn one daily merge into
a merge per push across thirty repositories.

The commit step is replaced with one canonical form rather than patched,
because the estate had two vintages of it — some repositories carry a
five-attempt push retry the template lacked, and re-emitting would have
deleted it. Both halves are here now.

The retry resolves the branch per run instead of resetting to a literal
origin/main. Eleven repositories in this estate have an agent branch as
their default, and there a rejected push would reset the checkout to a
different branch and push that over the deploy branch.

Unset ESTATE_DISPATCH_TOKEN means a delay of up to 24 hours, never a
loss — the daily merge is the floor, and the step says so loudly rather
than skipping green.

Kind: feature

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.title: Re-vendor shiplog: the filter learns directory/1, delivery/1 and intent/1
entries.detail:
Three formats gained a workflow that commits a refresh. Without this the
first run of each seals as work under agent/unattributed, inflating the
two numbers the record exists to make honest.

A vendored change does nothing until the copy is replaced, and a stale
copy does not fail — it disagrees, silently, about exactly the field
somebody has just changed.

Kind: chore

entries.title: Give this repository's directory fragment a machine that refreshes it
entries.detail:
shipped/1 and backlog/1 each ship a workflow with their adoption, so
every repository filing one has something re-running the emitter.
directory/1 never did — sixteen repositories in this estate got the
fragment and nothing else, and were still serving the bytes one
hand-sweep produced on 2026-08-31.

Nothing was red, and nothing would have gone red. A fragment nobody
re-emits does not decay for a year; it stops being true. A machine
surface added here never enters the graph, the asserted date freezes,
and a change to the vendored emitter reaches a copy that never runs it.

The workflow is generated by workflow() in @flashyos/directory rather
than hand-written, gates on the default branch resolved per run, and
commits with [skip ci] because a refresh is a record of what already
happened.

vendor-shiplog.mjs is re-vendored in the same commit: its bookkeeping
filter had never heard of "directory/1: refresh the fragment", so the
first refresh would have sealed as work under agent/unattributed.

Kind: feature

entries.title: Re-vendor check-directory.mjs: enforce what every edge type must carry
entries.detail:
The vendored checker had hand-written blocks for three of the sixteen edge
types and nothing for the other thirteen, so engaged without a basis,
delegatedTo without a scope and issued without a date all validated clean —
in thirty identical copies that agreed with each other perfectly.

It reads a requires table now, mirroring EDGE_REQUIRES in
@flashyos/directory, with one conditional: `declares` needs a role when it
names an agent and not when it names a machine surface. That split was
measured, not decided — across the estate all 88 agent declarations carry a
role and none of the 43 surface declarations do.

flashyos/tools/vendored-directory.test.mjs differentials this copy against
the package by verdict, and asserts every estate copy is byte-identical to
it. This repository's fragment passes the stricter checker unchanged.

Kind: fix

entries.title: Re-vendor the drifted copies [vercel skip]
entries.detail:
Two files, and one of them had never been compared. estate-hygiene compared
vendor-*.mjs and three check-* scripts; scripts/emit-frontdoor.mjs was carried
under its own name and matched neither pattern, so it drifted here unnoticed —
an emitter that disagrees with the estate's about what a door contains.

vendor-shiplog.mjs brings the hold applied at projection, so it can retract an
entry already sealed public, and a bookkeeping filter that tolerates the
[skip ci] suffix rather than sealing every refresh commit as shipped work.

Kind: fix

entries.title: A README for the repository, distinct from the org's front page [vercel skip]
entries.detail:
This repository had none, which matters more here than elsewhere: it holds
profile/README.md, the page GitHub renders at github.com/FlashyLabs, and
somebody looking for 'the README' finds a public marketing page and edits it.

Says which file is which, what the four record fragments are, and the two rules
that bite: vendor-*.mjs are byte-identical copies that disagree rather than
break when edited, and the fragments are generated.

Kind: docs

entries.title: Re-vendor the checkpoint emitter: an unused import was dropped
entries.detail:
Byte-identical to `packages/checkpoint/vendor-checkpoint.mjs` in flashyos,
which is the only way a vendored file is allowed to change. The difference
was one unused specifier, so nothing here behaved differently — which is
precisely why it sat undetected across thirteen repositories: a stale
vendored copy does not break, it disagrees, and only a byte comparison
notices before the disagreement matters.

Kind: chore

entries.title: Re-vendor the backlog emitter: it can revise an item now
entries.detail:
`file` has taken `--wants` since the beginning and nothing could add them
afterwards, so every item filed across the estate — all of them filed without
wants — was permanently invisible to the matcher, which refuses an item that
names no `capabilitiesWanted`. A format whose central field is
write-once-at-creation is a format whose central field is empty.

`revise` changes everything about an item except its visibility. Promotion
stays a separate verb because it is a separate decision: it refuses anything
but a `person/` id, and folding it in would give a revision the power to
publish. Unmentioned fields are left alone — `close` is a revision too, and
clearing on absence would strip every want in the repository.

Copied byte-identical from flashyos rather than edited here. A stale vendored
file does not break; it disagrees, silently, about exactly the field somebody
has just added.

Kind: chore

entries.title: Publish a directory/1 fragment, so this repository's signatures resolve
entries.detail:
Every sealed entry here carries `assertedBy: agent/<slug>-ci` and every filed
item carries `agent/<slug>-bot`, and nothing in the estate defined either. An
`assertedBy` naming an id nothing declares reads as provenance and carries
none, which is worse than leaving the field out — across the estate that was
2,478 edges citing identities that formally did not exist.

The repositories that already had a fragment each hand-wrote one around their
AAO charter. This repository has no charter, and neither will an outside
adopter of `shipped/1` on their first push, so the fragment comes from
`vendor-directory.mjs`: dependency-free, derived from the two config files
that already do the stamping, and validated here by the vendored checker.

It does not declare an organisation. `.shiplog/config.json` carries an `org`
field that adoption filled in with this repository's own slug, and in sixteen
repositories that names a company which does not exist. A repository is not
the authority for which organisation answers for it; defining one here to
raise a provenance number would put the fiction into the published graph. The
emitter says so on every run, and the gap is filed rather than papered over.

Kind: feat

entries.title: Carry the house rules, so an agent stops having to guess them
entries.detail:
Twenty of thirty-five repositories had no CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, and an
agent with no repository doc guesses. Every avoidable mistake made across
this estate on 2026-08-30 happened in a repository without one — and each
was a fact that is true everywhere rather than a fact about that
repository:

  work pushed to `main` in eleven repositories whose default branch is not
  `main`, deploying nothing and read by nobody, with the push succeeding;

  a vendored emitter trusted after its source changed, so a privacy hold
  added that morning did nothing in sixteen repositories and published the
  entry it was meant to withhold;

  a copyright holder guessed as the studio on a client's site;

  measurements reported from a working copy while claiming to describe the
  branch that ships — twice, in two tools, by two agents, four hours apart.

None of that is repo-specific knowledge, and writing it thirty-five times
would drift the first time it changed. It is declared in
`tools/estate-house-rules.mjs` in flashyos and synced between two markers.
Everything outside the markers is this repository's own and is never
touched.

Where this file is new it says the repository is not yet described, which
is true. A generated description would be wrong and would read as
authoritative; admitting the gap is a task somebody can close in a minute.

Kind: docs

entries.title: Name a copyright holder, and stop granting what was never ours
entries.detail:
Two errors from the licence sweep of 2026-08-30, found by putting the
estate's licences in one register and comparing.

A LICENCE THAT NAMED NOBODY

Eleven repositories carried a bare Apache-2.0 text with no copyright line
at all. That is not a missing file — it is a file that answers the
question wrongly. It reads as a grant, and no reader can tell who made it
or whether they were entitled to. Every LICENSE now opens with the holder
and one line saying what the repository is.

AN OPEN LICENCE ON SOMEBODY ELSE'S PROPERTY

kopman-build and buildos are a construction firm's marketing site and the
application behind that engagement. Both carried AGPL-3.0-only, which
offers a client's own site to anyone willing to publish their changes.
Nobody decided that; it was the default that got reached for. Both are now
all rights reserved, held by Kopman Build, with a line saying ownership is
governed by the agreement between the firm and the studio rather than by
the file.

The same care had already been taken for marco.law an hour earlier and
then not taken here, which is the argument for a register rather than for
being more careful next time.

Eight further repositories moved from an unattributed Apache-2.0 to all
rights reserved: the org profile, the Terraform that can delete
production, three brand properties and the three Life repositories.
flashy-sdk is among them and its package.json already said UNLICENSED —
the LICENSE file had been contradicting its own manifest.

`tools/estate-licences.mjs` in flashyos is now the one declaration, and it
reports a checkout and a default branch separately, because conflating
those is the mistake this estate's tooling keeps making.

Kind: fix

entries.title: Re-vendor: carry the emitter this repository is actually meant to run
entries.detail:
`estate-hygiene`'s vendored-emitter check found five copies behind the
package they came from. This is the same class of failure the check was
written for, caught this time before it did anything: a per-entry privacy
hold added to the emitter on 2026-08-30 did nothing in sixteen
repositories carrying a copy from an hour earlier, and marked the held
entry public.

A stale vendored file does not break. It disagrees — silently, and about
whichever field somebody has just changed.

Kind: fix

entries.title: Adopt checkpoint/1 alongside the other two
Declare a licence: Apache-2.0
entries.detail:
The organisation profile. Its only code is the vendored emitters, which are
Apache-2.0 where they come from, so copyleft here would attach to nothing of
ours.

An absent licence is not permissive; it is all rights reserved by default.

Kind: docs

entries.title: Re-vendor the emitter, and publish this log
entries.detail:
The vendored copy here predated four changes: an emit that unions rather
than replaces, a per-entry privacy hold, a guard that stops an agent's
commits being filed under a person, and a filter for this format's own
refresh commits.

A stale vendored copy does not fail. It disagrees with the source about
what it was told to do — which is how a hold added this morning did
nothing in sixteen repositories and marked the held entry public.
estate-hygiene now compares every vendor-*.mjs byte-for-byte against the
package it came from, and this repository was one of nine it caught.

visibility is public. Everything derived has been private since adoption;
this is the decision that makes it a changelog anyone can read.

Kind: fix

entries.title: Adopt shipped/1 and backlog/1
entries.detail:
The org profile repository is public-facing — it is what a stranger sees on the
organisation's GitHub page — so a change to it is worth recording, and the
hygiene check now asks any repository with content for a record rather than
only one with source files.

One entry, sealed. Filed under `org/flashylabs` and `repo/flashylabs-github`:
the name `.github` is a convention every owner shares and identifies nothing on
its own, so the owner is the identity here.

Kind: feature
